sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:1
items.html:
Any image or form whatsoever: For all these discernments that we discern in the worlds flow and issue from the world of Atzilut downward, that is, from the world in which ten Sefirot and the correction of the lines have already been revealed, in the secret of Hesed, Din [judgment] and Rachamim [mercy]. Indeed, above the world of Atzilut, that is, before the ten Sefirot were revealed, we have no grip there at all, such as to discern there any resemblance or disparity of form between one Sefira and another, because the beginning of attainment begins from the clothing of the ten Sefirot in ten vessels, that is, from the world of Atzilut downward.
And this is what the ARI writes, that we have no power to engage with what precedes the emanation of the ten Sefirot, nor to picture any image or form whatsoever; for before the emanation of the ten Sefirot, which were revealed in the world of Atzilut, the ten Sefirot were considered as light without a vessel fit for it, and it is known that we have no attainment of light without a vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:2
items.html:
Speak by way of allegory and likeness: Meaning that from the world of Atzilut downward it is possible for us to hint at the discernments that are in the upper spiritual roots above, by way of allegory and likeness taken from the reality or from the conducts of this world; for all the particulars of the creatures and the modes of their conduct that are found in this world cascade and are drawn from the upper worlds, exactly like the relation of a seal to the imprint made from it, in which all the particulars found in the seal are transferred and pass over into the imprint made from it, so that not even a trifle is missing.
And this is what our sages said: “There is not a single blade of grass below that has no angel appointed over it from above, who guards it and strikes it and says to it, ‘Grow.’” (Beresheet Rabba, Portion 10; Zohar, Omissions to Part 1, Item 61) They teach us by this that there is no small particular in this world that has no root in the upper world, and that this root acts upon it in its whole form and in all its inclinations, in everything that it does here before our eyes in this world. Therefore the sages found for themselves a special language in which to transmit their attainment of the upper worlds, in writing and orally, from generation to generation: namely, that they take the branches that are in this world and explain by means of them the reality in the upper worlds to which those branches correspond.
And since the said relations of root and branch begin only from the world of Atzilut downward, that is, from the time of the revelation of the completion of the ten Sefirot, and not at all before that, it is self-understood that it is entirely impossible to hint at the reality of these upper ones with the help of the corporeal branches, for these branches have no direct relation to them such that they would be fit to explain their concepts.
And this is what the ARI writes, that what he speaks here too by way of allegory and likeness is only in order to settle the ear. That is, to give us a grip on some trifle, so that he may be able to show us the roots of the world of Atzilut; in such a way that first one must understand the branch in its relation to its root in Atzilut, and afterwards it is possible to relate this root to its own prior root, which is in the worlds that precede Atzilut.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:3
items.html: The ten Sefirot of Atzilut: Which are the matter of the expansion of spirituality, called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida (NRNHY), and the matter of vessels and organs, called KHB, HGT, NHYM, or the five Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf]: AA, AVI and ZON, in which the NRNHY clothe. And each of these matters is a study of its own, meaning that the ways of its cascading and of its revelation differ from those of the other; and not only that, but they are opposite to one another from one extreme to the other. For in the vessels, the upper vessels are revealed first — first Keter [crown] is revealed, afterwards Hochma, and last Malchut — and the opposite is the case in the lights, in which the lower ones are revealed first: first Nefesh is revealed, afterwards Ruach, and last Yechida. And so they are opposite to one another in all their appearances and phases. Therefore, if we do not know well the reasons of the matters from their root, we cannot escape becoming confused in this wisdom. And this is what the ARI writes: “and therefore we must speak in the order of the degrees from beginning to end.” That is, for then we shall understand well the reasons of each and every matter from its root, and it will be possible for us to understand and to distinguish, in every degree, the modes and the orders that are in the vessels as befits them, and the modes and the orders that are in the lights as befits them, and the concepts of the one will not be interchanged with those of the other.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:4
items.html:
Akudim, Nekudim and Berudim: These are the names of the three first worlds that cascaded one from another until ten Sefirot were emanated as they should be, that is, ten lights called Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama, Haya, Yechida, clothed in ten vessels called Keter [crown], Hochma, Bina, Hesed, Gevura, Tifferet, Netzah, Hod, Yesod, Malchut.
And at first only one vessel was emanated, which is called the vessel of Malchut, in which all the ten lights were clothed and tied in that one vessel alone. For this reason that first world is called by the name world of Akudim, from the word Akud, meaning bound and tied, as this matter is written further on. And it is also called one line, or the world of Adam Kadmon. It is called one line because the light is clothed in one vessel only, and there are not yet in it the three lines of the conduct, which are called Hesed, Din [judgment], Rachamim [mercy]; for this vessel is termed the quality of Din, which is the vessel of Malchut.
Indeed, afterwards an association was made with the quality of Rachamim; that is, Malchut, who is termed the quality of Din, was included and associated with each and every Sefira of the nine Sefirot that precede her, which are termed the qualities of Rachamim. Through this association a vessel was made in each and every Sefira, and then the ten Sefirot were completed as they should be, and then the three lines of the conduct, called Hesed, Din, Rachamim, were made in the ten Sefirot.
And this is what our sages said: “At first it arose in the thought to create the world with the quality of Din, and He saw that the world would not endure, and He gave precedence to the quality of Rachamim and associated it with the quality of Din.” (Beresheet Rabba, end of Portion 12) At first glance this saying is hard to comprehend: are His thoughts in any way like the thought of flesh and blood, who at first wishes to do thus, but then regrets it for some reason and does otherwise? Indeed, we have already explained (see Part 1, in the explanation of the words “before” and “afterwards”) that the matter of “at first” and “afterwards” that is stated in spirituality means cause and consequence, where the cause is called “before,” and the consequence drawn from it is termed “afterwards.”
And this is what our sages made us hear: that the first cause of the worlds, called the first world, was emanated and came out in the phase of the vessel of Malchut alone, which is termed the quality of Din; but “He saw that the world would not endure,” meaning that there is not in this that perfection which is desired from the creation of the world, and therefore “He arose and associated it with the quality of Rachamim,” meaning that this therefore became the factor from which the matter of the association of the quality of Rachamim with Din would follow, and because of this ten Sefirot, lights and vessels, came out and were emanated, as above, in the three lines HDR. And our sages hinted at that same matter in another place with a change of wording (Avot, beginning of Chapter 5): “With ten utterances the world was created; and could it not have been created with a single utterance? Rather, in order to exact punishment from the wicked, who destroy the world that was created with ten utterances, and to give a good reward to the righteous, who sustain the world that was created with ten utterances.” Ten utterances means ten Sefirot, as is known. And they ask: since the primordial world was created in the secret of a single utterance, that is, in the secret of one vessel alone, in the vessel of Malchut, as above, why then did ten Sefirot cascade and come out of her? And to this they answered, “in order to exact punishment from the wicked,” etc., “and to give a good reward to the righteous.” That is, because the thought of the creation, which is in order to delight His creatures, is not realised in any other way than through the conduct of reward and punishment, that is, ten Sefirot, which is the secret of the conduct of the three lines: Hesed, Din, Rachamim. And therefore the primordial world, where there was nothing but the vessel of Malchut alone, was compelled to cascade from state to state until the ten Sefirot were emanated, which is the secret of the association of the quality of Rachamim with Din, as above, which reveals the conduct of reward and punishment that brings about that benefaction included in the secret of the thought of creation, as explained.
And behold, the beginning of the said association was made in the world of Akudim itself, through the refinement of the coarseness in the screen; and by reason of this three Partzufim came out and cascaded there, which are termed Galgalta, AB, SAG. And although they are all still the phase of Akudim, nevertheless the matter of the association comes to be in them by degrees, as is written below. And afterwards the Partzuf BON of AK came out, which is called the world of Nekudim, where the three lines HDR were emanated in the ten Sefirot of the first three, KHB, which is termed Rosh [head]; but in the ZAT, ten Sefirot had not yet come out except in one line only. And in that world there was the matter of the breaking of the vessels.
And this breaking of the vessels became the cause for the matter of the association of the quality of Rachamim with Din to be completed, in the phase of the three lines HDR and ten complete vessels, also in the seven lower Sefirot, HGT NHYM, which are in the world after it, called the world of Berudim, and the world of correction — for the reason that the correction of the world according to the thought of creation begins precisely from this world and not before it.
And thus the difference between the three worlds mentioned in the words of the ARI has been explained: the world of Akudim means that the ten lights were bound and tied in one vessel only. Whereas in the world of Nekudim, in the phase of its first three, KHB, the association of the quality of Rachamim with Din has already been made in it. And only in the world of Berudim, which is called the world of Atzilut, was it corrected there, and the matter of the association of the quality of Rachamim was completed in it entirely, also in the seven lower Sefirot, so that there is here a clothing of ten lights inside ten vessels. And from that world the matter of the discernment of ten Sefirot in actual fact begins.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:5
items.html:
The surrounding lights joined inside the Peh: You already know that the Peh [mouth] is the secret of the Malchut of the Rosh [head] of AK, in whom a screen of phase four was corrected, which restrains the upper light from expanding and clothing in her fourth phase. For it is the way of the upper light to come and expand also in phase four, and to fill the whole of reality as before the restriction; only, the screen corrected in the Peh restrains it, and she does not receive it — and this is called a coupling by striking, as is known. And then, the whole measure of the upper light that is fit to come and clothe in phase four, and which she does not receive, as said — behold, this upper light returns backward to its source and becomes a garment upon the first nine Sefirot of direct light (and see above, Part 3, Chapter 12, and in the Inner Light, ibid.). Thus all the lights destined to come into the worlds after the completion of their correction, which are termed surrounding lights, are included in this reflected light that clothes the first nine Sefirot of direct light of the Rosh of AK; for this is the upper light that is not received in phase four, and therefore it does not fill the whole of reality as it did before the restriction. Indeed, through all the couplings and the reflected light destined to be revealed in the worlds by the raising of MAN from the deeds of the righteous, phase four turns out to be corrected, until she will be fit to receive the light as she was in Ein Sof [infinity] before the restriction — as it is written in the Zohar, “Ein Sof did not lower His unity upon her until they gave Him His mate,” which is the secret of the correction of phase four, as explained. (And see Shaar HaKavanot, on Aleinu LeShabeach.)
And behold, it has been explained that all the surrounding lights are included in the screen and in the reflected light that are in the Peh of the Rosh of AK, together with the inner lights, which are the nine Sefirot of direct light that are tied in her. And this is what the ARI writes: the inner light with the surrounding lights joined inside the Peh, that is, Malchut, by the force of the screen of phase four corrected there, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:6
items.html: Outside the Peh tied together: Both the inner light and the surrounding light are tied in phase four: for the first nine Sefirot of direct light are tied and clothed in her reflected light, and these are what is called inner light. But the lights destined to come until the end of correction, which are called surrounding light, are also included in this reflected light, for they are the very substance of the reflected light, as above; and because of this they are destined to be revealed little by little in the course of the six thousand years, and after them until the end of correction (see above item).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:7
items.html: Strike one another and clash with one another: For when the two lights descend and expand from the Peh [mouth] downward into the Guf [body] of AK, behold, the surrounding lights cannot clothe inside the Guf, because of the force of the screen that is there, which restrains that light, as above. (And see Part 2, answer 4.) And since they are tied and included there, they too wish to expand into the internality of the Partzuf, and therefore they thereby refine the coarseness in the screen, that is, that same force of restraint which does not let them clothe there. Indeed, by the force of this clash of theirs against the coarseness in the screen, whereby the screen is progressively refined because of them, this causes the departure of the inner lights from the Guf. For when it is refined to the coarseness of phase three, the reflected light is shortened and clothes only the level of Hochma, and the light of Keter [crown] disappears from the Guf. And when phase three too has been refined to the coarseness of phase two, the reflected light is shortened to the level of Bina, and the light of Hochma too disappears, etc., until all the coarseness has been refined and there is no longer any coupling by striking there, and all the inner light disappears from the Partzuf. And this is what the ARI writes, “they strike one another and clash with one another,” meaning that the one rejects the other: for the whole greatness of the inner light lies in the greatness of the coarseness in the screen, as above, and therefore it grows stronger in greater coarseness. And conversely, the whole restraint upon the surrounding lights, which cannot clothe, comes only from the force of the coarseness and the limitation in the screen, and therefore it progressively refines the coarseness. And therefore they clash with one another until both of them depart, as explained. (And see the General Preface in my books on Etz Chaim.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:8
items.html:
Before the existence of Akudim: Akudim are the phase of the ten Sefirot of the Toch of the first Partzuf in the reality that is after the first restriction, which is termed Adam Kadmon; for before that there was no phase of Rosh [head], Toch, Sof [end] at all in the upper light, but rather the upper light filled the whole of reality (as is written well in Part 1).
And this is what the ARI writes, “before the existence of Akudim” — that is, in the ten Sefirot that are in the Rosh of Adam Kadmon, which precede the ten Sefirot of the Toch of Adam Kadmon that are called Akudim — “the upper light could not clothe in any vessel.” And this is well explained in Part 3: that there is no phase of a vessel at all in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, but only roots for vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:9
items.html: The vessels had no capacity to bear it: For the reflected light that rises from Malchut upward is not considered a vessel of reception for the upper light, but only a root for a vessel of reception. Therefore, so long as the Malchut of the Rosh [head] does not expand and widen into ten Sefirot of her own and within her, through the reflected light that turns about and descends from above downward, there are no vessels there at all (and see above, Part 3, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3); for the reflected light rises there from below upward, and every clothing that is from below upward indicates the phase of departure from reception. And the reason we call this a clothing is that the ten Sefirot become tied there and become a root for clothing. And this is what the ARI writes, that the vessels had no capacity to bear it. Understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:10
items.html: Until the expansion of that great light reached the phase of Akudim: Until Malchut and the reflected light that is with her draw the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head] into the Toch from above downward, as above; and then the phase of one vessel is made, that is, the vessel of Malchut, who expanded and widened and received into herself the whole quantity of light with which her reflected light clothed the ten Sefirot of the Rosh (and see Part 3, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3). And these ten Sefirot, which descend from the Rosh downward and clothe in the vessel of Malchut that has widened, are the very ones called the ten Sefirot of Akudim, or the world of Akudim.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:11
items.html: The emanation began to have in it some existence of a limitation of the light: For the Malchut at the end of that vessel, who is discerned as the Malchut of the vessel of Malchut, is the one that limits the upper light on its way, so that it will not expand from her downward; and this force of limitation is termed by the name Tabur, or Hazeh [chest].

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:12
items.html:
Which could not have been the case until now: That is, although the Malchut of the Rosh [head] also limits the upper light — for that is why a coupling by striking and a raising of reflected light are made there (as above, Part 3, Chapter 1, Inner Light, Item 70) — nevertheless this limitation and this reflected light of the Malchut of the Rosh are not considered a limitation in actuality at all, but only the phase of a limitation in potential, as the ARI writes in Etz Chaim, Gate 42, that Keter [crown] is like the matter called Hyle, in which there is the root of all four elements, in potential and not in actuality, etc.; and therefore it is possible to call it Ein Sof [infinity] and Emanator. And his intention is to the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, which is called Keter, as is known.
Yet these words of the ARI are deeper than the deepest, and indeed they must be understood, since they deal with the root of the wisdom and with its beginning. For one must understand very well the difference between “potential” and “actuality,” which the ARI states in order to divide between the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, which are clothed in reflected light that is from below upward, and the ten Sefirot of the Guf [body], which are clothed in reflected light that is from above downward — to the point that the ten Sefirot of the Rosh are for this reason sometimes called Ein Sof and Emanator with respect to the ten Sefirot of the Guf.
And the matter is that there is a very great difference and distance between the reflected light that rises from the screen in Malchut upward and clothes the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, and the reflected light that descends together with the direct light from the ten Sefirot of the Rosh downward to the Guf, so much so that they appear to be opposite to one another. For the reflected light that rises from below upward is not only not discerned as a vessel of reception for the direct light that it clothes, but there is even in it an opposition to reception, since everything from below upward means that the light turns to the Emanator and not to the receivers. Indeed, even so the rising reflected light becomes a garment upon the upper light — that is, it becomes a root for the connection of the upper light with the emanated being — because the vessel of the Malchut of the Rosh, who raised that reflected light, turns out to expand and widen through it, of her own and within her, and becomes a vessel of reception which is termed the Guf of the Partzuf (as above, Part 3, Chapter 2, Inner Light, Item 3), so that the ten Sefirot of the Rosh descend from above downward and expand and clothe inside her.
And you see that although the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, by their own nature, withdraw from coming into a vessel of reception — for such is the meaning of the reflected light that rises from below upward, namely to the Emanator and not to the emanated beings, as written above — even so, all the light that is actually received in the Guf comes only from the ten Sefirot of the Rosh that expand within it from above downward, as explained in Item 30.
Therefore the ten Sefirot of the Rosh are discerned as having ten Sefirot “in potential and not in actuality,” meaning that the matter of the actual clothing of the light in vessels is not found in the Rosh at all, but only the phase of the potential and the root from which that clothing will be drawn; and therefore the Rosh is called by the name Ein Sof, or Keter. Understand this very well.
And this is what the ARI writes, “and then” — that is, after the light expanded in the Guf of the Partzuf, which is called Akudim — “the emanation began to have in it some existence of a limitation of the light, which could not have been the case until now.” That is, that before Akudim, namely in the Malchut of the Rosh, there could be no existence of limitation there; for as to Malchut limiting and raising reflected light in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, this limitation is actual bestowal, since the greater the limitation, the greater is the measure of bestowal in it: for the limitation of phase four draws the level of Keter, while a limitation smaller than it, that is, phase three, draws only the level of Hochma. And therefore no limitation whatsoever is discerned in the Rosh.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:13
items.html: Ten lights: That is, only after the two Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf], AB and SAG of AK, were revealed and came out, in which the light entered and left the vessel ten times; for through these entries and exits the discernment of ten lights distinct from one another was made, as is written below.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:14
items.html: The force of these ten lights was in them at first: Before they expanded into Akudim, that is, in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh [head], where the ten Sefirot are discerned as being only in potential and not in actuality (as above, this chapter, Item 30).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:15
items.html: The light was not limited inside the vessel: And this limitation begins to be revealed only through the coupling by striking and the risings of reflected light from below upward of the second look, which comes after the clothing of the light in the emanated being, that is, after Akudim, as is written further on. This is not so through the first look, which is in the Malchut of the Rosh [head]: there the light is not limited, as written above. Remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:16
items.html: The existence of their being ten was not yet discernible: And even in the expansion that is from the Rosh [head] downward it is likewise not discernible that they are ten lights; rather, the ten lights are considered as one light. This is because the whole discernment in the lights comes only from the phase of the vessels in which they clothe, and since there is here as yet only one vessel, the ten lights too are considered as one light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:17
items.html: Akudim, which is from the Peh to the Tabur: The Malchut of the Rosh [head] is termed Peh [mouth], and the Malchut of the Guf [body] is termed Tabur. The first nine Sefirot of the Guf begin to expand from the Peh, that is, from the Malchut of the Rosh, and they end at the Tabur, which is the Malchut of the Guf. And the whole place from the Tabur downward until the Sium of the Guf is discerned as the Sefira of Malchut alone. And although from the Tabur downward ten Sefirot are likewise discerned, they are the phase of reflected light and of female light, and they are discerned as receivers that cannot bestow. Therefore the expansion of the direct light from the Peh downward is discerned only as far as the Tabur, and there it stops, because of the screen that is found there in the Tabur.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:18
items.html: And after He drew it, that light departed and rose again: And this is in the secret of the second look, as is written above in the words of the ARI (Part 3, Chapter 12), which comes after the light has been drawn into the vessel, and not before that, as written above (in the Inner Light, Chapter 7, Item 60).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:19
items.html: To its source in the Peh: She is the Malchut of the Rosh [head], which is termed Peh [mouth], and she is considered the source and root of all the light that expands in the Guf [body] of the degree, for it is she who drew it through the first look (Part 3, Chapter 12) that is made in her.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:20
items.html: For the cause of the expansion of the light and of its departure afterwards: For the essence of a vessel is made through the record that remains after the departure of the light, as is explained here in the words of the ARI; and if so, the two of them are equal in the making of the vessel. Therefore two couplings are needed here, which are called the first look and the second look: for the first look is for the expansion of the light, and the second look is for the departure of the light; and through these two phases of coupling the vessels of reception of the degree are completed. And this is the secret of the verse, “as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, so the Lord will rejoice,” etc. For “rejoiced” and “will rejoice” mean coupling, and there is an upper coupling to destroy, which means the departure of the light, just as there is an upper coupling to do good, which means the expansion of the light, as above; and therefore both of them are termed rejoicing.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:21
items.html: All at once and in a single moment: And although couplings by striking are made there in the course of the departure of the light, and because of this four levels of ten Sefirot come out, one above the other, as is written further on, nevertheless it is considered one departure in a single moment, because the upper light couples with the screen in the course of its refinement and disappearance; and therefore these couplings are not discerned as expansion.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:1:22
items.html: According to the distance of those parts one from another: And you will understand this from what is written in Part 1 (in the Inner Light, page 4, Item 50), that in the upper light itself four phases are discerned — HB TM — even before it expands into a coupling by striking. And behold, because of this the one vessel too was imprinted with those four phases, HB TM, that are in the light. Therefore ten Sefirot are discerned in that one vessel as well, that is, according to the distance of those four phases one from another. Indeed, since there is here only one vessel, which is Malchut, as above, for this reason the light too is considered one light, without any discernment of ten Sefirot, for the reason that we have no grasp of the light except from the modes of its clothing in vessels; and since the vessel is one, we find that the light too is one.
